Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:23: Indeed, the arguments he said to his heart are two: the first, that He would not have chastised us out of hatred for us, for if so He would have destroyed us - and this is a sign that He chastises us out of love, as it says (Psalms 118:18), "the LORD has chastised me sorely." And the second, that He renews the work of creation every single day continually, and this is complete kindness - and all the more so will He fulfill His word, which He spoke through His servants the prophets, to gather us from the four corners of the earth - to this point. And when you examine his words, you will find them close to the view of my teacher that I wrote, concerning the reason why one who acts out of love merits the supernal pleasantness, as I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:24: And on the Mishnah "any love that is dependent on something - when the thing ceases, the love ceases," he wrote, in these words: this hints that one who serves the Blessed Name in order to increase his possessions and preserve his soul - his service is not complete, as Satan said (Job 1:9), "does Job fear God for nothing? Have You not made a hedge about him?" And to this the Tanna said that one who serves the Name for the sake of physical things upon which he has made his service dependent - his service will not endure to shine with the light of life, for when those things upon which his service depends cease, his love ceases - and "there is no eating or drinking in Sheol, where you are going." But one who serves the Name with complete love - behold, his love is in the life of the worlds and will never depart, and his reward is that he will love the Name forever, as it is said, "and their crowns on their heads," enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:25: And the Tanna explains and says: which is love not dependent on anything? This is the love of David and Jonathan. The intent is that it is said of them (I Samuel 18:1), "and it came to pass, when he had finished speaking, that the soul of Jonathan was bound with the soul of David," and so on; and likewise it is said (ibid. 20:41), "and they kissed one another and wept, one with the other, until David exceeded." And there is no kissing except from the side of love, and weeping from the side of cleaving; and "until David exceeded" is because it is the secret of the exile of the Shechinah - and David and Jonathan hint at the secret of love in the secret of "dodim" [lovers] above, and the discerning will understand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:26: And in the Zohar they explain, concerning the secret of love, a hidden and concealed secret, and we will copy his words, in these words (Shemot 146a): concerning what King Solomon said (Song of Songs 1:2), "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - what did King Solomon see, that he introduced words of love between the upper world and the lower world, and that the beginning of the praise of love that he introduced between them is "let him kiss me"? Rather, it has already been established, and this is so: there is no love of cleaving, spirit to spirit, except through a kiss - and a kiss is on the mouth, the source of the spirit and its outlet; and when they kiss one another, these spirits cleave to one another and become one, and then it is one love. In the book of Rav Hamnuna Sava, of old, it said concerning this verse: the kiss of love spreads to four spirits, and the four spirits are as one, and they are within the secret of faith, and they ascend through four letters, and these are the letters upon which the holy Name depends - the upper and lower [worlds] depend on them, and the praises of the Song of Songs depend on them; and what is this? Love. And they are the supernal chariot, and they are fellowship and cleaving and the completeness of everything - these four letters are [also] four spirits, and they are spirits of love and gladness in all the limbs of the body, without any sadness whatsoever - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:27: My teacher, peace be upon him, explained this discourse in his commentary on the Sava (Zohar, Mishpatim 124b), and likewise in the Zohar in the passage mentioned. Indeed, let us explain what pertains to our subject in this exposition: that the reality of the virtue of love is the bond of four spirits, formed in the secret of the kisses; and the secret of the kisses is explained there in the passage further on: "who will kiss me?" - that One who is concealed within the supernal concealment. And the secret of the kiss is the cleaving of the inner essence of the sefirot and their inwardness, which is the spirit of life that gives them life - and this is what it says, "and a kiss is on the mouth, the source of the spirit and its outlet." And so it says (Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs 63a): "in the Song of Songs, the cleaving of body to body [is external]; 'let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth' is the cleaving of spirit to spirit" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:28: How there are these four spirits is explained there, in the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs 64a), in these words: "let him kiss me" - cleaving in love, spirit to spirit - for four spirits join together and become one: this one gives its spirit to its fellow and receives the spirit of its fellow, cleaving to it; the spirit of this one and the spirit of its fellow are found, that makes two - and so too its fellow - so four spirits are found joining together in these kisses - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:29: And it says at the end of the discourse we copied: "and they are spirits of love and gladness in all the limbs of the body, without any sadness whatsoever." The explanation: it is impossible for [these spirits] to cleave through the inner spirit unless the sefirot bind together as one from the side of their externality, and judgment, which is their sadness, diminishes - then there is a throne on which the supernal spirit may rest upon them. And this is like the parable of a man kissing his beloved: he kisses her only out of abundant joy, and all his limbs have already been unified as one - and this is the word "ahavah" [love], which adds up [in gematria] to "echad" [one], indicating the bond and unity of the created, caused things with one another through their inner spirit and soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:30: And it also explains in the discourse that the letters of "ahavah" are the letters upon which the holy Name depends, and they are the letters of the Name YHVH. And my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote and drew a correspondence between the letters of "ahavah" and the letters of YHVH - and through this we may understand why, in most of the verses in the Torah, it is written "to love YHVH."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:31: And now we must understand how, in the reality of a person's love for the Holy One, blessed be He, four spirits are found. And the matter is that a person's soul is a portion of God from above; and when a person prepares his body and his limbs together, and arouses his heart in joy - for the Shechinah does not rest amid sadness - and directs his intention to arouse the love of his Creator within his heart, then necessarily a supernal spirit is aroused within his heart, and a holy flow is drawn into him - behold, this makes two. And this is the matter of "let him kiss me" - that the spirit of the male comes down below to perform kisses; and afterward he directs his intention to be included and to cleave his soul above - behold, this makes two spirits above. And this reality of the two [pairs] happens of itself, like "as face answers to face in water," which I explained above - and thereby love is complete, four spirits joining together as one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:32: And the matter is further explained in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Pekudei 226b), in these words: this sixth Heichal is [the place of] kisses, to cleave spirit to spirit, lower to upper, as it says (Song of Songs 1:2), "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - and every kiss is to cleave spirit to spirit, upper within lower. And it says further on: and this is the secret - when spirit unites with spirit, then the kisses begin to join, and the rest of the limbs are aroused in response, and this spirit cleaves to that one; and then all the limbs are aroused, one to another, to bind limb to limb. And should you ask, which arouses which - do the lower limbs arouse, or the upper limbs? The lower limbs are always aroused toward the upper ones - one who is in darkness always yearns to be in light; the black flame below is always aroused toward the white flame above, in order to cleave to it and rest beneath it - and this is the secret of (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not keep silence; do not hold Your peace, and do not be still, O God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:33: And although it appears at first glance that this discourse disagrees with what is explained in the Song of Songs [passage], which says that the kisses are the cleaving of the upper spirit within the lower - this is not a difficulty. For the intent of this discourse in Parashat Pekudei, which says that the kisses are to cleave spirit to spirit, lower within upper, means that the yearning of the lower spirit is to be included in the upper - and this is what "let him kiss me" means: that the lower spirit be included in the upper. However, it is impossible for the lower to be included in the upper unless the kiss of the male comes first and its spirit is included within it - and through the striking of that illumination, there is power in the lower spirit to be included in the upper. And in order for that illumination to come from the male, the arousal of the female must first come, as it is written, "the lower limbs are always aroused toward the upper ones."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:34: And along these lines is the reality of love in a person: for first he must have his yearnings come before, to cleave to the supernal light; and once the Holy One, blessed be He, sees his yearning appearing [manifesting] within him, from His supernal light, through this his soul also becomes included above, and four spirits are found binding together as one above - a doubled bond in reality, like "as face answers to face in water," which I explained in the first chapter - that when a person arouses love of his fellow within his heart, his fellow's love is also aroused in his own heart, and so two spirits are found in each one - and this is the secret of the words of Rabbi Yosi, "spirit draws spirit and brings spirit," which I explained in chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:35: And through this may also be understood what they said (Yoma 39a): a person who sanctifies himself a little is sanctified much more - for the bond is doubled, as we explained, and he cannot easily be separated from the sanctity of His love, blessed be He, because the King has also seized him with cords of love, and therefore he is sanctified greatly. And this is like the parable of one who binds his fellow with a rope to draw him near - and once his fellow sees that he wishes to bind him, what does he do? He too throws a rope toward him, and they draw near to one another quickly, and are bound together with one strong and firm bond, between which there is no separation at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:36: And one who merits this love is, without doubt, bound and cleaved to the supernal life, and happy is he in this world and the World to Come. And of this it is said, "to love the LORD and to cleave to Him" - and this is the secret of "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive today," as I explained in chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:37: And so too, in the Zohar (Mishpatim 124b), they explain the verse "but you who cleave" concerning the secret of the kisses, in these words: and therefore it is written, "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - for this is cleaving, spirit to spirit. It is taught: all the while the Holy One, blessed be He, walks with Israel, as it were, spirit cleaves to spirit - and therefore it is written, "but you who cleave to the LORD your God," in all those aspects of cleaving, and this does not separate from that - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:38: And after we have explained that love is the kisses, it is fitting to explain whether they are found in Binah and in Chesed. And kisses that are found in Binah are explained in the Song of Songs [passage] (Zohar Chadash 64a), in these words: "with the kisses" - from those supernal kisses that were kissed previously - for the love of joy comes only from within the kisses, the cleaving of the upper spirit within the lower. "His mouth" [pihu] - and it is not written "his mouth" [piv, without the extra letter] - what is "pihu"? Rather, this is the preparation of the World to Come, the King to whom all peace belongs - and this is the added heh, added to this, because all the love of the lower world is only to join with the upper world, the World to Come - and therefore every praise arouses the lower world toward the upper world - to this point. Behold, it is explained that kisses come from the side of the supernal heh, the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:39: And that kisses are an arousal from the side of Chesed is explained in Parashat Terumah, there, in these words: once he enters the Heichal of Love, the love of the supernal kisses is aroused, as it is written, "and Jacob kissed Rachel" - to be the kisses of supernal love as is fitting; and these kisses are the beginning of the arousal of all the love of cleaving and binding above - to this point. And it is necessarily inferred from the substance of this discourse's language that this mentioned "Heichal of Love" is Chesed within Atzilut - and so my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, saying that from it the love of the kisses is aroused.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:40: It remains now to explain what is explained in the Zohar, that love is from the side of the supernal Imma. The reason is that when a person considers the abundant goodness of the Creator, blessed be He, toward him, of which he cannot count one part in a thousand of His goodness toward us in the matter of his creation, his soul yearns to serve Him out of love - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Tanchuma (see Emor 7), on the verse (Job 41:3), "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" In these words: Rabbi Yirmiyah ben Elazar said, in the future a heavenly voice is destined to burst forth on the mountaintops and say, whoever has worked with God, let him come and take his reward; and the holy spirit cries out and says, "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" Who praised Me before I placed a soul in him? Who circumcised himself before I gave him a son? Who made tzitzit before I gave him a garment? Who made a parapet before I gave him a roof? And they elaborate there similarly on every matter - it is upon Me to repay his reward. Why? "Under the whole heaven it is Mine" - for everything is Mine, and I give from what is Mine, and nevertheless, "I will repay" - it is upon Me to repay his reward - to this point. And this Midrash is brought in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat "Shor O Chesev" (27:2); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:41: And when we consider the words of this discourse in the way of the secret, "mi" [who] is Imma, corresponding to the fifty gates of Binah that spread from her to do good to all creatures - as it recounts in the passage where "the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind" (Job 38:1), which mentions fifty "gates" [i.e., instances of the word "mi," "who"]: "who has set its measures, if you know," or "who has stretched a line upon it" (ibid. 38:5); "who has cleft a channel for the flood" (ibid. 38:25); or "who has begotten the drops of dew" (ibid. 38:28); "out of whose womb comes the ice" (ibid. 38:29); "who provides food for the raven" (ibid. 38:41); "who has sent out the wild donkey free" (ibid. 39:5) - the general point being that fifty gates are mentioned there, as the Ra'avad, peace be upon him, explains in his commentary on Sefer Yetzirah (Introduction). It follows from this that the Holy One, blessed be He, went ahead and opened fifty gates of His goodness to do good to all creatures, and therefore He says, "who has preceded Me" - for by the attribute of "mi" [Binah], no creature preceded Me; rather, "mi" came first and gave him a soul and all goodness. And this is why Binah is called "kedem" [before/ancient], for it preceded the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 3), concerning the seven things created before the world was created, one of them being the Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 8:22), "the LORD acquired me as the beginning of His way, before His works of old" - and it says "kedem," meaning before the world was created. And likewise the Garden of Eden, as it is said (Genesis 2:8), "a garden in Eden, kedem" - before the world was created. And this is because "olam" [world] refers to the six extremities, and what precedes the world of six is Binah, and therefore it is called "kedem" - as Rabbi Moshe de Leon and my teacher explain in Sefer Pardes Rimmonim. And nevertheless, "it is upon Me to repay" - for the good reward of the righteous is "to gaze upon the pleasantness of the LORD," drawn from her - and this is "it is upon Me to repay" - along the lines of "al HaShem" [i.e., "concerning/upon the LORD"] (Zohar III, 79b, on I Samuel 1:10).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:42: And concerning our subject, that we explained that love is drawn from Imma, who is the heh: when a person considers that the Holy One, blessed be He, created him and formed and sealed his body and spirit with the 22 holy letters, which are from the side of Imma, and through them is the mold of all the worlds - it is fitting that he love Him and perform His will, especially since she is the mother who bestows good kindnesses on her children, as explained in the Sefer HaBahir (see section 105); and this is "heh" - five lights of the first day, as explained in the Tikkunim (4b, 19a), which come to Chesed and are the root of the fifty gates. And so too, in the Zohar (Vayetze 154a) and in the Song of Songs [passage] (Zohar Chadash 62a), they elaborate on the matter of Binah, that it is a place that requires joy, where there is no anger or judgment at all, for the World to Come is entirely joy, and it rejoices for everyone, sending joy and gladness in every direction - to this point. And so it is a river that flows and goes forth and whose waters never cease (Zohar, Bereshit 33b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:43: And further, in another distinction, it is fitting that love be designated for Binah, because through the answering of our prayer in all our troubles - as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:7), "for what great nation is there that has God so near to them, as the LORD our God is whenever we call upon Him?" And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va'etchanan (265a), that there is a distinction between "the LORD your God" [singular "your"] and "the LORD our God" - that "the LORD your God" is the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, while "the LORD our God" is Abba and Imma. It follows from this that fear is when a person fears the Emanator, who is the Creator of all, great and ruling, and this fear of his is revealed to a person through Abba, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2; and love is when a person loves the Creator of all from the side of His kindnesses and His goodness toward him, and the revelation of this love to a person is revealed through Imma, as we explained - and the essence of love is the arousal of the heart in desire, as will be further explained, with God's help. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in tractate Kallah (chapter 3): what is love and what is honor? Love is in the heart, and honor is in deeds and words - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:1: Although the nature of love has been explained in the previous chapters, it still remains to explain further its nature, and how a person may cleave to it in such a way that it never departs from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:2: And concerning the nature of love, Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explains, in these words (Zohar, Acharei Mot 67a): Rabbi Abba said to him, (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul desires You in the night; my spirit within me seeks You early" - "desires You" [avitecha] - it should have said "You" [otecha]; "seeks You early" [ashacharecha] - it should have said "he shall seek You early" [yeshacharecha]. Rather, it has already been established, as it says (Job 12:10), "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all human flesh." Come and see: nefesh and ruach are always partnered together. It is taught: the complete service that a person must perform for the Holy One, blessed be He - as we have learned (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God" - is that he should love the Holy One, blessed be He, with a literal love of the soul; and this is the complete love, the love of his soul and his spirit. Just as these [nefesh and ruach] cleave to the body, and the body loves them, so a person must cleave, to love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of his soul and spirit, to cleave to Him - this is what is written, "my soul desires You in the night," meaning my very soul; "my spirit within me seeks You early," to cleave to You with abundant love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:3: "In the night" - for a person must, out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, arise every single night to engage in His service, until morning breaks and the thread of Chesed is drawn upon him - for it is taught, happy is the portion of that person who loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with this love; and these are the true righteous who love the Holy One, blessed be He, thus - for the world endures for their sake, and they rule over all the harsh decrees above and below, because the world endures for their sake. It is taught: that righteous person who cleaves with his spirit and soul above, to the holy King, in love as is fitting, rules over the earth below, and everything he decrees upon the world comes to pass - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:4: And explaining "desires You" [avitecha] - it should have said "You" [otecha] - the intent is that the plain sense of the verse appears to be that the nefesh desires the Holy One, blessed be He, at night, and through the ruach within it, it seeks the Holy One, blessed be He, early. And he raised a difficulty with this: since "desires You" and "seeks You early" refer to the nefesh and the ruach, it should have said "my nefesh, You" and "my ruach shall seek You early." And to this he answered that "my nefesh" and "my ruach" do not refer only to the nefesh and ruach in man, but also to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, who are also called "nefesh" and "ruach," from whom the [human] nefesh and ruach come - as he writes further on: "come and see, nefesh and ruach are always partnered together." And the reason they are partnered in the world is that just as their root comes from above, from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and one is impossible without the other - as it is said (Psalms 89:15), "righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" - so too the branches coming from them are partnered. And therefore they said in the Tikkunim (49b), on the verse (Proverbs 20:27), "the candle [ner] of the LORD is the soul [neshamah] of man" - "N-R" is nefesh-ruach, "neshamah" is neshamah - behold, nefesh and ruach are partnered as one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:5: And he brought the verse "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing" to show that although the ruach and the nefesh descend and are clothed in the body, their root remains above, and through that root that remains there, He literally has in His hand "the soul of every living thing." And this matter is a preparation for the matter of love that he will explain afterward, and to resolve the difficulty of "desires You" - it should have said "You" - and to this he said that if the intent were toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah alone, it should have said "O LORD my God, I desire You in the night, I also seek You early" - but rather, to teach us the matter of the love and cleaving of a person's soul to the Holy One, blessed be He, how it is, he said "my nefesh" and "my ruach."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:6: And further, he intended to bring this verse to resolve what the verse says, "my spirit within me [bekirbi] seeks You early" - for according to his explanation, that this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, it should have said "my spirit also seeks You early," for the word "bekirbi" [within me] is superfluous. To this he intended to bring this verse, "in whose hand," to show that literally a spark of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is within a person, and the souls are threads of flame drawn from above to below, and they have no life except from their root, which flows into them forever; and when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to remove [His] assistance from the lower nefesh and ruach, He removes the root bound with it, so that it no longer flows life to the lower nefesh and ruach, and immediately the person dies - as it is written (Job 34:14-15), "if He should set His heart upon him, He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul; all flesh would perish together." And this "gathering" is thus: that He gathers his spirit to Himself, similar to one who smells an apple or the like, drawing that scent in and gathering it to himself - so the ruach and nefesh are gathered to their source.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:7: And so Rashbi explains (Zohar, Vayechi 217b): Rabbi Yehuda said, happy are the righteous when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to return their spirit to Him, to draw in that spirit into Himself - for it is taught, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to return his spirit to Him, if he is righteous, what is written (Ecclesiastes 12:7)? "And the spirit shall return to God who gave it" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:8: It follows that while a person lives, a spirit of life from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is within him, giving him life - and this is "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing," to flow life; He withdraws it all according to His will. And with this the word "bekirbi" [within me] is resolved, referring both to the nefesh and to the ruach emanated from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah. And the sense of the verse is thus: "my nefesh desires You in the night" - "my ruach" too, meaning the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and they are within me ["bekirbi"] - "I seek You early." And "I seek You early" means to engage in His service until morning breaks, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:9: And behold, with this introduction we may understand the verse (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people [ammo], Jacob is the lot [chevel] of His inheritance" - we must understand what "portion" [chelek] means and what "lot" [chevel] means, and why it says "ammo" [His people] rather than "Yisrael." And it is possible to understand this through what we have explained - that when we say "portion" [chelek], it indicates that souls are hewn from Him, and He and they are two portions, along the lines of the "two halves of a body" - and this is the nature of the word "chelek," that the thing is divided from it; and when the portion of the lower soul is unified with Him, the two portions are unified and become one. And although it says "portions," indicating, Heaven forfend, separation, the intent is not that the soul is separated from Him upon its descent below, but rather that its root remains there - and therefore it says "ammo" [with Him/His people] - literally with Him is the portion, and therefore it does not say "for the LORD's portion is Yisrael," which would indicate that the portion was divided below and would indicate separation - but rather "ammo" - meaning that those who are with Him are with Him. And to indicate the doubled bond - He, blessed be He, also flows a spark of life to the lower ruach and nefesh in the body, and it is never separated - to this he says, "Jacob is the lot [chevel] of His inheritance" - for just as a rope [chevel] is woven from two or three strands, so He is bound with us below and we are bound with Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:10: And further, in the parable of the rope, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Bamidbar Rabbah 17:6) a pleasant matter concerning the commandments, and we copied their words in a chapter of the first Gate, the Gate of Commandments - saying there a parable of one who was cast into the water; the captain extended a rope to him and said to him, take hold of this rope in your hand and do not let go of it, for if you let go you have no life. So the reality of the soul is let down from above to below like this rope - one end in His hand, and the other end in a person's body - and the entire reality of love and cleaving is to cleave to this rope and bind to the root of one's soul, which is cleaved to Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:11: And with this the language of the discourse may be understood: "it is taught, the complete service that a person must perform for the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have learned, 'and you shall love the LORD your God,' is that he should love the Holy One, blessed be He, with a literal love of the soul - just as these cleave to the body and the body loves them, so a person must cleave," and so on. The intent is that the verse (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul," means that he should love Him with a literal love of the soul - and its explanation is that the love of the soul for the body is a doubled love, for the soul loves the body and the body loves the soul, and they do not wish to be separated from one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:12: And the love of the soul for the body, the verse teaches us, when it says (Song of Songs 8:6), "for love is as strong as death." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Vayechi 245a) that at the hour of a person's death, the soul is torn from the body like a person going on a long journey and separating from his beloved, for whom this separation is difficult - in these words: "set me as a seal upon your heart" - so that your whole image remains within you, like this seal, whose whole image remains in the place to which it is applied. "For love is as strong as death" - it is as intense as the separation of the spirit from the body, for it is taught, at the hour a person is about to depart the world, and sees what he sees, the spirit goes through all the limbs of the body and its wheels ascend, like one going in the sea without oars, ascending and descending, and it does not help him; it comes and is torn away from all the limbs of the body, and there is no intensity like the day the spirit separates from the body. The intensity of the love of the Community of Israel for the Holy One, blessed be He, is like the intensity of death at the hour the spirit wishes to separate from the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:13: "Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol": whoever loves and is not bound with jealousy, his love is not [true] love. Once he is jealous, behold, his love is complete. From here we learn that a person must be jealous for his wife, so that a complete love be bound with her - for through this he will not set his eyes on another woman. What is "jealousy is as cruel as Sheol"? Just as Sheol is cruel in the eyes of the wicked who must descend into it, so jealousy is cruel in the eyes of one who loves and is jealous, at the [thought of] separation from love - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:14: And this is what the discourse before us said, "just as these cleave to the body" - this is the love of the soul for the body, that it is cleaved to it and does not wish to separate from it, for once it is clothed [in it], it has a relationship and closeness with it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:15: "And the body loves them" - this is the love of the body, because it has no life except through it [the soul] - for just as it is hard in the eyes of the Shechinah to separate from the Holy One, blessed be He, to the point that she says, "set me as a seal," in a reality where it is hard for the spirit to separate from the body - with such love the soul of the righteous must be bound to the Shechinah. And this is what it says, "and then a person must cleave" - with this reality, he should love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of his soul and his spirit, to cleave to Him: just as he loves his own spirit and soul in his body, through which he lives, so he should love the Holy One, blessed be He, and cleave to Him with the portion of his lower spirit and soul - for in truth they have no life except through the flow of the supernal roots cleaved to Him, blessed be He, through which the Name sends life to the lower branches in the body, as we explained. And so it says at the end of the discourse, "that righteous person who cleaves with his spirit and soul above, to the holy King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:16: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the discourse of Vayechi that we copied, that among the signs of love is jealousy - and he explains that one who is jealous for his wife, because his abundant love for her, does not want a stranger to intrude between them to separate him from her, but rather wants his wife's love to be bound to him forever. So too the righteous man, out of his abundant love for the Shechinah, must bind himself in her love to such an extent that he becomes jealous for her, not wanting the Shechinah to separate from him and rest upon another, in a way that would uproot her from him - and this is the reality of "the love of his soul and spirit, to cleave." And the sign of the reality of this love is that he rises at night to occupy himself with Torah, as he will explain further on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:17: And the second distinction, which is the love of the soul for the body, is also explained of itself - for certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, loves him, since He gives him the soul from Himself so that he may live; and it is fitting that he say in his heart: just as the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to cleave to me, since He gives me spirit and soul and flows life to me, so it is fitting that I cleave to Him - and to this he says "the love of his soul and his spirit," without qualification, which is a doubled love, as we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:18: This is what is written (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul desires You in the night" - my very soul, for He, blessed be He, is the essence of the soul, since the lower soul is one branch of the supernal root that is within it; and further, He is literally the soul itself, for without His vitality there is no soul. It follows that one who loves his soul and spirit, repairing them through the performance of Torah and the commandments, loves the Holy One, blessed be He - and from the affirmative you may infer the negative [i.e., one who does not so occupy himself does not truly love Him].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:19: And it says "in the night" - for a person must, out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, arise every single night. The matter of this love is like the parable of a man who loves his beloved: at night, when he is aroused, he is aroused with the desire of her love, and hastens to the time of his desire for her with great love, especially when he knows that his beloved loves him. So too Torah scholars, who abstain from their wives on all weekdays because of the "time" of the daughter of the King, who is the Torah - it is fitting that they hasten with desire for the Torah, for in occupying themselves with it they cleave to the supernal life, and they cleave to the Shechinah, and she comes and flows from her holy spirit upon them. And the Shechinah's love for us needs no proof, for she says (Song of Songs 8:13), "you who dwell in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice; let me hear it" - and this is why the prophet calls the Shechinah "my soul" and desires her, because she is the holy spirit that comes and rests upon him.
